evidence: src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: `if (product.availableStock < quantity) throw new DomainError(`Insufficient stock for product ${productId}`)`
src/domain/product.ts: `if (quantity > this.stock) throw new InsufficientStockError(this.id);` inside Product.reserve

src/domain/errors.ts: `class InsufficientStockError` builds the message `Insufficient stock for product ${productId}`, and `class NotFoundError extends DomainError` is never used inside the domain module
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: `if (!product) throw new DomainError(`Product ${productId} does not exist`)` in reserve and release
src/domain/order-status.ts: `nextStatus` / `canTransition` leave out the cancelled transition
src/domain/order.ts: Order.cancel hard-codes `this.status === "shipped" || this.status === "delivered"` outside order-status.ts
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The files cover one domain concern: orders, products, stock and their repositories. They do not always use the module's own abstractions, though.

1. Duplicated stock check: in stock-reservation-service.ts, `reserve` runs its own check, `product.availableStock < quantity`, and throws `new DomainError(`Insufficient stock for product ${productId}`)`. `Product.reserve` in product.ts already owns this rule (`if (quantity > this.stock) throw new InsufficientStockError(this.id)`). So the rule lives in two places, and the service skips the dedicated `InsufficientStockError` type. It even copies that error's message text into a plain `DomainError`. Code that branches on the error type will treat these two failures differently.

2. Unused not-found error: errors.ts defines `NotFoundError`, but stock-reservation-service.ts reports missing products with plain `DomainError(`Product ... does not exist`)` in both `reserve` and `release`.

3. Split transition rules: order-status.ts holds the transition table (`nextStatus` and `canTransition`), which leaves "cancelled" out. `Order.cancel` in order.ts then hard-codes its own rules (`status === "shipped" || status === "delivered"`). The order state machine is therefore defined in two files rather than one.

violations.message: Repeats the stock-sufficiency rule already enforced by Product.reserve (`product.availableStock < quantity`) and throws a generic DomainError with InsufficientStockError's message text instead of the InsufficientStockError type.
Reports missing products with a generic DomainError instead of the NotFoundError defined in src/domain/errors.ts.

Order.cancel hard-codes its own status rules (rejects shipped, delivered and cancelled) instead of keeping them in the transition rules in order-status.ts (nextStatus/canTransition), so the order state machine is defined in two files.
